GOOGL.rationale: GOOGL's core business is genuinely strong: revenue accelerated +24.2% YoY to $119.8B in Q2 2026, operating margins expanded to 34.0%, and Google Cloud surged 82% to $24.8B with a $514B backlog. The balance sheet is a fortress ($242B cash, ~0.44 D/E). However, the headline 18x PE is deeply misleading — Q2 net income of $112.19B includes a ~$99B one-time gain on equity securities (SpaceX/Anthropic stakes), inflating EPS to $9.11 vs. ~$2.85 adjusted. On normalized operating earnings, the stock trades at a mid-to-high 20s PE, consistent with its recent range, so there is no meaningful valuation discount vs. its own history. The near-term picture is complicated by negative FCF (-$5.8B in Q2), capex guidance raised to $195-205B (more than double 2025), the end of the $346B buyback program, and the Gemini 3.5 Pro delay. Berkshire Hathaway's $31B+ position provides institutional validation and is a modest positive signal, but the capital-cycle intensity and antitrust overhang (DOJ structural remedies) temper enthusiasm. The stock has declined ~6.4% since April despite the strongest revenue quarter, suggesting the market is correctly looking through headline EPS. Mildly positive: a high-quality franchise with real growth, but no clear mispricing and meaningful near-term headwinds from the spending cycle and FCF turn.
